Team — I ran the numbers and sketched three viable pool options. Putting the rationale inline for transparency; attaching a formal proposal PDF.

Option A — Conservative (lower commit)
- Pool: 3x H100-style instances (high-memory flavor), each node: 80GB VRAM
- Expected sustained throughput: ~45–55 req/s (600 tok avg) with p99 ~500–600ms
- Monthly commit (reserve): 3 nodes * 24/7 * 730h = 5,220 node-hours
- Pricing: list rate (no discount) yields higher per-token cost; good for POC.

Option B — Recommended (balance of cost and latency)
- Pool: 5x H100-style nodes with KV-cache enabled and int8 quantization for the model family you plan to serve
- Expected sustained throughput: ~95–125 req/s (600 tok avg), p99 ~280–350ms with continuous batching and prefix cache
- Monthly commit: 5 * 730 = 3,650 node-hours (note: we size committed capacity for average sustained load; burst handled by burst pool)
- Pricing: 12mo commit -> 30% discount off list Dedicated rate; 24mo -> 38% discount. We recommend 12mo minimum to validate production SLAs.

Option C — Aggressive (high throughput, lower unit cost)
- Pool: 8x H100 nodes + optional sharded KV cache (for very high token footprints)
- Sustained throughput: ~160–200 req/s, p99 ~220–300ms
- Monthly commit: 8 * 730 = 5,840 node-hours
- Pricing: 24mo -> 42% discount + potential upfront consumption credits.

Operational notes / guarantees:
- We can commit to provisioned throughput SLOs tied to pool size; formal SLO metrics and penalty credits will be in the SLA addendum.
- Autoscaling for burst (short term) will be available but priced as on-demand (metered) capacity; we can set a predictable burst budget per month.
- For PHI, recommend Private deployment (VPC) or Dedicated with strict network controls; Security will send compliance docs.

See attached: Dedicated_proposal_2026-08.pdf (contains cost tables, sample SLA language, and a visualization of token latency vs concurrency).

-Marissa
